title: Nebbiolo
description: Also called Spanna and Chiavennasca. Piedmont's noble grape: pale in colour, high in tannin, scented with roses and tar.
L: Nebbiolo gives pale ruby to garnet wines with aromas of rose, violet, red cherry, tar, liquorice and dried herbs, often summed up as tar and roses. It has very high tannin and high acidity, with medium to high alcohol. Its pale colour hides its power, a classic surprise in blind tasting.
Tar and roses, high tannin and acid

Nebbiolo's name may come from nebbia, fog, which covers the Langhe hills in autumn when it's harvested, often in October. Or from the white bloom on its berries, like a fog. It's one of the first grapes to bud and the last to ripen, so it needs the warmest, best-exposed slopes. Its skins are low in stable colour pigments, hence the pale colour.
Why is Nebbiolo pale despite being very tannic?
Its skins are low in stable colour pigments
Nebbiolo has plenty of tannin but few stable pigments, so the colour is light.

Look for pale ruby with an orange or brick rim, even when quite young. On the nose, rose, cherry, tar and herbs. On the palate, a striking grip of tannin with high acidity. A pale red that grips like Cabernet is almost certainly Nebbiolo.
Nebbiolo is one of the first grapes to ripen.
Not true. It buds early but ripens very late, often in October.
Nebbiolo smells of tar and roses, with very high tannin and acidity
Its name may come from nebbia, the autumn fog

Nebbiolo's heart is the Langhe and Roero, around Alba, in Piedmont. Barolo and Barbaresco are its great wines. Roero, across the Tanaro river, makes lighter, more perfumed Nebbiolo on sandy soils. Langhe Nebbiolo and Nebbiolo d'Alba are more affordable regional wines.

In northern Piedmont, Nebbiolo is called Spanna and grows in Gattinara, Ghemme, Boca and Lessona, on volcanic and acidic soils, giving fresher, more mineral wines. In Lombardy's Valtellina, it's called Chiavennasca and grows on steep Alpine terraces. Valle d'Aosta's Donnas also uses it.
Match each name or place to Nebbiolo.
Nebbiolo has several homes in northern Italy.

Nebbiolo is very site-specific: it needs warm, sunny slopes, often south-facing, and calcareous marl to show its best. Plantings in California, Australia and Argentina exist, but few match Piedmont. It's one of the least travelled great grapes.
What is Nebbiolo called in Valtellina?
Chiavennasca grows on Valtellina's steep Alpine terraces.
Nebbiolo's heart is the Langhe and Roero
It's Spanna in northern Piedmont and Chiavennasca in Valtellina
It's very site-specific and rarely succeeds abroad
Explain the MGA system and the Barolo wars

Barolo DOCG covers 11 villages south-west of Alba. Two soil types matter: Tortonian marl, in the west around La Morra and Barolo, gives more perfumed, softer wines; Serravallian sandstone and marl, in the east around Serralunga and Monforte, gives more powerful, tannic wines. Barolo must be 100% Nebbiolo.

Barolo must age at least 38 months, 18 in wood; Riserva 62 months. Since 2010, labels can name 181 MGAs, Menzioni Geografiche Aggiuntive, the officially defined vineyard areas, like Cannubi, Brunate and Monprivato. They work like Burgundy's crus.
Which part of Barolo gives the most powerful, tannic wines?
Serralunga and Monforte, in the east
Serravallian soils in the east give more structure.

From the 1980s, modernists, like Elio Altare, used short maceration and new French barriques for softer, fruitier Barolo. Traditionalists, like Bartolo Mascarello, kept long maceration and large old Slavonian casks, called botti. The debate split the region. Today many producers blend both approaches.
Match each term to its meaning.
Barolo's 11 villages split into Tortonian and Serravallian soils
It ages at least 38 months; labels can name 181 MGAs
The Barolo wars pitted barriques against botti
Describe Langhe Nebbiolo and northern styles

Barbaresco DOCG covers three main villages, Barbaresco, Neive and Treiso, north-east of Alba, near the Tanaro river. It's slightly lower and warmer, so Nebbiolo ripens earlier. Barbaresco must age at least 26 months, 9 in wood; Riserva 50 months. It has 66 MGAs, like Rabajà and Asili.

Barbaresco is often described as more elegant and approachable earlier, with softer tannins, while Barolo is more powerful. In practice, site and producer matter more than the name. Angelo Gaja, from the 1960s, raised Barbaresco's prestige worldwide. The Produttori del Barbaresco co-operative is renowned for quality.
Barbaresco must age longer than Barolo.
Not true. Barbaresco needs 26 months; Barolo 38.

Langhe Nebbiolo and Nebbiolo d'Alba offer younger, fruitier versions. Roero gives perfumed wines on sand. Gattinara and Ghemme in the north are fresher, more mineral. Valtellina's Sforzato is made from dried grapes, like Amarone. Together they show Nebbiolo's range.
Barbera d'Asti is made from Barbera.
Barbaresco ages 26 months and is often more elegant
Gaja and the Produttori raised its prestige
Langhe, Roero, Gattinara and Valtellina show Nebbiolo's range
Describe how it changes with age

Nebbiolo's very high tannin and acidity make young Barolo and Barbaresco firm, even harsh. Over years, tannins polymerise, linking into longer chains that feel softer. Acidity preserves freshness. Traditionally, Barolo needed 10 years or more before it was ready.

Young Nebbiolo shows red cherry, rose and fresh herbs. With age, it fades to garnet and brick, and develops tar, leather, truffle, dried roses, tobacco and forest floor. The finest can last 30 to 50 years. Modern winemaking has made many approachable sooner, but the best still reward patience.
What happens to Nebbiolo's tannins over time?
Tannins bind into longer chains that feel smoother.
Decant young Barolo for several hours before serving. Old Barolo needs only a short, gentle decant to remove sediment.
Order these colours as a Nebbiolo ages.
Nebbiolo starts pale and turns orange-brown with age.
Nebbiolo's high tannin and acidity need time to soften
With age it develops truffle, tar and dried roses
The finest Barolo lasts 30 to 50 years
Choose the right Nebbiolo for the occasion

Nebbiolo suits Piedmont's rich food: tajarin pasta with butter and white truffle, brasato al Barolo, beef braised in Barolo, roast game, and aged cheeses like Castelmagno. Truffle and Nebbiolo share earthy aromas. Its tannin and acidity cut through richness.

Serve at 17 to 18 degrees in a large glass. Decant young wines for hours. Langhe Nebbiolo can be drunk young, within five years. Barbaresco often from 7 to 20 years, Barolo from 10 to 30 years or more. Choose the younger styles for everyday meals.
Which dish is a Piedmont classic with Barolo?
White truffles from Alba are in season from October to December, the same time Nebbiolo is harvested. That's no coincidence for Piedmont's cooking.
Delicate fish would clash with its tannin.
Nebbiolo suits truffle, braised beef and aged cheese
Serve at 17 to 18 degrees in a large glass
Choose Langhe Nebbiolo for youth, Barolo for patience
Tar and roses is its classic description.
Match each wine to its rule or place.
A pale colour in Nebbiolo means low tannin.
Not true. Nebbiolo is pale yet very tannic.
Which develop in Nebbiolo with age?
Green apple is a young white wine note.
Barolo labels can name official vineyard areas called ____.
Nebbiolo is pale but highly tannic and acidic
Barolo and Barbaresco are its great wines
It needs time; the best age for decades
It suits truffle, braised beef and aged cheese
